goal.source: IEA World Energy Balances 2024, world total final consumption and electricity
goal.method: Every scenario stops where electricity reaches 35% of final energy demand: electricity is today's plus the electricity the assets add (e), demand is today's minus the fuel they replace (f) plus e. The chart's energy axis writes the same condition as 65% e + 35% f against the gap below, so f and e, and the total energy at the stop, differ by scenario.

scenario_labels.usd_cost__bau: Cost-optimized scenario, lowest USD cost [BAU Grid]
scenario_labels.usd_cost__clean: Cost-optimized scenario, lowest USD cost [Clean Grid]
scenario_labels.usd_hybrid__bau: Cost-optimized scenario, savings ranked by USD cost [BAU Grid]
scenario_labels.usd_hybrid__clean: Cost-optimized scenario, savings ranked by USD cost [Clean Grid]
scenario_labels.lowest_cost__bau: Best value per tonne of emissions scenario [BAU Grid]
scenario_labels.lowest_cost__clean: Best value per tonne of emissions scenario [Clean Grid]

scenario_rules.usd_cost__bau: Each asset takes the strategy with the lowest cost in USD (net present value, not divided by the reductions; ties: the larger reduction); assets are ranked by that USD cost, lowest first, so the strategies that save the most money come first. Only strategies that reduce emissions can be picked. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.usd_cost__clean: Each asset takes the strategy with the lowest cost in USD (net present value, not divided by the reductions; ties: the larger reduction); assets are ranked by that USD cost, lowest first, so the strategies that save the most money come first. Only strategies that reduce emissions can be picked. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.usd_hybrid__bau: Like the Best value per tonne of emissions scenario (ranked by cost abatement, but every sector takes its lowest-cost strategy), except that strategies with a negative cost (they save money) are ranked by their USD cost (net present value) instead of their cost abatement: each asset takes its cheapest strategy on that basis (savings first, the largest saving first; then the lowest cost abatement; ties: the larger reduction), and assets are ranked the same way. Only strategies that reduce emissions can be picked. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.usd_hybrid__clean: Like the Best value per tonne of emissions scenario (ranked by cost abatement, but every sector takes its lowest-cost strategy), except that strategies with a negative cost (they save money) are ranked by their USD cost (net present value) instead of their cost abatement: each asset takes its cheapest strategy on that basis (savings first, the largest saving first; then the lowest cost abatement; ties: the larger reduction), and assets are ranked the same way. Only strategies that reduce emissions can be picked. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.average__bau: The base case (BAU Grid only): each asset takes an average solution, built from all the strategies it could take (those that reduce emissions with a clean grid). Its reduction, energy electrified and cost (net present value) are the averages over those strategies, and its cost abatement is the average cost divided by the average reduction. Assets are ranked by their average reduction, largest first. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.reductions__bau: Each asset takes the strategy with the largest emissions reduction, with no country or cost limit; assets are ranked by reduction, largest first. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached. The same strategies can be picked under both grids (those that reduce emissions with a clean grid); under BAU Grid their reduction can be zero or negative, but the energy electrified is the same.
scenario_rules.reductions__clean: Each asset takes the strategy with the largest emissions reduction, with no country or cost limit; assets are ranked by reduction, largest first. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached. The same strategies can be picked under both grids (those that reduce emissions with a clean grid); under BAU Grid their reduction can be zero or negative, but the energy electrified is the same.
scenario_rules.lowest_cost__bau: Each asset takes the strategy with the lowest cost abatement (ties: the larger reduction); assets are ranked by cost abatement, lowest first, so the cheapest tonnes come first. Buildings (residential and non-residential) take their second-lowest cost abatement strategy instead, which usually replaces more energy; road transportation and iron and steel take the lowest, and an asset with a single strategy keeps it. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached. Cost abatement is net present value ÷ annual reductions, in $ per tCO₂e per year (Clean Grid or BAU Grid, as selected). The same strategies can be picked under both grids (those that reduce emissions with a clean grid); under BAU Grid their reduction can be zero or negative, but the energy electrified is the same.
scenario_rules.lowest_cost__clean: Each asset takes the strategy with the lowest cost abatement (ties: the larger reduction); assets are ranked by cost abatement, lowest first, so the cheapest tonnes come first. Buildings (residential and non-residential) take their second-lowest cost abatement strategy instead, which usually replaces more energy; road transportation and iron and steel take the lowest, and an asset with a single strategy keeps it. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached. Cost abatement is net present value ÷ annual reductions, in $ per tCO₂e per year (Clean Grid or BAU Grid, as selected). The same strategies can be picked under both grids (those that reduce emissions with a clean grid); under BAU Grid their reduction can be zero or negative, but the energy electrified is the same.
scenario_rules.cost_100__clean: Cost-effective reduction: only strategies with a cost abatement of at most $100 per tCO₂e per year can be picked (cost abatement = net present value ÷ annual reductions, Clean Grid or BAU Grid as the scenario); among them each asset takes the one with the highest reduction, and assets are ranked by reduction, largest first. Assets with no strategy under the cap are not selected. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.cost_150__clean: Cost-effective reduction: only strategies with a cost abatement of at most $150 per tCO₂e per year can be picked (cost abatement = net present value ÷ annual reductions, Clean Grid or BAU Grid as the scenario); among them each asset takes the one with the highest reduction, and assets are ranked by reduction, largest first. Assets with no strategy under the cap are not selected. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.
scenario_rules.cost_250__clean: Cost-effective reduction: only strategies with a cost abatement of at most $250 per tCO₂e per year can be picked (cost abatement = net present value ÷ annual reductions, Clean Grid or BAU Grid as the scenario); among them each asset takes the one with the highest reduction, and assets are ranked by reduction, largest first. Assets with no strategy under the cap are not selected. The goal tab shows where the 2024 target is reached.

scenario_order.usd_hybrid__bau: strategies that save money first (lowest USD cost first), then lowest cost abatement
scenario_order.usd_hybrid__clean: strategies that save money first (lowest USD cost first), then lowest cost abatement
